changes: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts: DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions() now calls settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(false) before settingsManager.reload(), so the trust bootstrap always resolves extensions with untrusted project settings even when the settings manager previously held a trusted state.

validation.notes: Root cause: the bootstrap pass in DefaultResourceLoader.loadProjectTrustExtensions forced setProjectTrusted(true), contradicting its own comment and the documented contract. With a previously trusted settings manager, the bootstrap reloaded settings trusted, packageManager.resolve() returned project-scoped resources, and project extensions were loaded and handed to resolveProjectTrust before any trust decision. Fix is the single-value change to setProjectTrusted(false); no other production code touched. The regression loads the real production module via .prale-eval/subject.mjs with its settings/package/extension boundary fakes and asserts three things: (1) reload({resolveProjectTrust}) with initialTrusted: true delivers a bootstrap extensions result containing user.ts and cli.ts but not project.ts, and the event log shows ['set', false] then ['settings', false] strictly before the first ['resolve', false], while the post-decision trusted reload still yields user.ts, project.ts and cli.ts; (2) a second reload after a trusted reload again bootstraps untrusted (['resolve', false]) with no project.ts; (3) calling loadProjectTrustExtensions() directly on a trusted loader leaves state.trusted === false and returns only user.ts and cli.ts. Reverting the one-line fix made the script fail with an assertion (project extensions must not load during the trust bootstrap, got ["cli.ts","user.ts","project.ts"]), and with the fix it exits 0. Limitation: node_modules is absent in this workspace, so the repository's vitest suites (and type checking via tsgo) could not be executed; focused validation is the standalone Node 24 VM-modules regression plus source review of package-manager-cli.ts, which already constructs its settings manager with projectTrusted: false and therefore aligns with the corrected contract.
